correctness.rationale: Ultrahomogeneity of the countable universal r-uniform hypergraph for integer r>=2 makes each injective labeled n-tuple orbit an arbitrary r-edge incidence pattern, exactly I_r(n)=2^{C(n,r)}. Every ordered tuple has a unique equality partition into k blocks, followed by one injective k-tuple orbit, so T_r(n)=sum_k S(n,k)2^{C(k,r)}. Reindexing j=n-k yields exact positive collision layers S(n,n-j)2^{-D_{r,j}}, D=C(n,r)-C(n-j,r)=sum_{t=0}^{j-1}C(n-t-1,r-1). To bound remainder after fixed m, near-diagonal Stirling coefficients satisfy S(n,n-j)<=n^{2j}; for j in [m+1,n/2] the extra successive D increments are Omega(n^{r-1}), giving geometric tail; for j>n/2 the n^n partition bound is negligible against 2^{-Theta(n^r)} when r>=2. Thus remainder O(n^{2m+2}2^{-D_{r,m+1}}). At m=1 the first correction binom(n,2)2^{-C(n-1,r-1)} and next-layer error follow. The inverse expansion uses delta^2=O(error). The n=0 conventional counts are 1; the result states the fixed-n formulas naturally. Independent computations for r=2..5,n<=10 verify Stirling identities, and the actual artifacts/verify.py independently enumerates equality patterns; finite checks cannot prove the asymptotic.
